newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly up on spread action.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly up on spread action.

text.p: Short covering lifted CME live cattle futures from early lows and spread action kept most at net gains into the close, traders said. Feeder cattle were knocked lower by weaker cash feeder cattle prices and an upturn in feed costs, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.175 cent per lb lower to 0.175 higher with only December off and February up most at 63.425 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.600 cent lower to unchanged with January off most at 65.225 cents.
December live cattle were weighed down by the less than expected $65 per cwt cash sales Tuesday. This also prompted some rolling of longs into February, traders said.

But hedge lifting curbed the setback in December while bull spreading bolstered February. February held technical support before firming on short covering and spreading. Trading was overall light as the market awaited Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report and the upcoming holidays, they said.
Estimates on the cattle report for feedlots of 1,000 head or more in the seven key states averaged 103.2 percent of last year for on-feed numbers as of December 1, in a range of 102 to 104.2 percent.
November placement estimates averaged 105 percent in a range of 98 to 110 percent and marketing forecasts averaged 93.9 percent in a range of 91 to 98 percent of last year.

R.J. O'Brien and Cargill Investor Services bought December early while Refco and RBH sold. RBH later turned a buyer in December and also bought February along with E.D.&F. Man and R.J. O'Brien. ADM Investor Services sold, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, hedging in April and June were noted early, as was buying of April 64 puts and selling of 68 calls and buying of June 60 puts and selling of 64 calls. Later, Cargill bought February 62 puts while commission houses and commercial bought February 60 puts, pit sources added.
Feeders remained under pressure from higher corn futures and a decline in the latest CME feeder cattle index.

Traders noted that feeders opened down on sell stops and remained weak after falling through technical support Tuesday. January and March fell through 40-day moving averages on the recent setback, traders said.
The latest index slipped $0.11 to $65.47 per cwt.
E.D.& F. Man and Chicago Corp sold January while local short covering limited the setback in January.
Stone Traders bought January feeders and sold June live cattle while E.D.&F. Man bought August feeders and sold August live cattle, pit sources said.
